problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})={e}^{x}+1$ and $L({y}_{2})=2{e}^{x}-3$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L(2{y}_{1}-{y}_{2})?$

feedback.problem:
Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})={cot}^{2}⁡x$ and $L({y}_{2})=3{csc}^{2}⁡x-4$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L(4{y}_{1}-{y}_{2})?$

*Hint: Use ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta =1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta .$*
feedback.worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
L(a{y}_{1}(x)+b{y}_{2}(x))=aL({y}_{1}(x))+bL({y}_{2}(x))
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L(4{y}_{1}-{y}_{2}) & =4L({y}_{1})-L({y}_{2}) \\  & =4\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡x-(3{csc}^{2}⁡x-4) \\  & =4{cot}^{2}⁡x+4-3{csc}^{2}⁡x \\  & =4(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)-3{csc}^{2}⁡x \\  & =4{csc}^{2}⁡x-3{csc}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={csc}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
